intro: This awareness course builds foundational understanding of learning disability and autism; it is not the Oliver McGowan Mandatory Training.
points: Watch for diagnostic overshadowing: never dismiss a treatable illness as simply part of someone's learning disability or autism.
This is awareness only; it does not replace the Oliver McGowan Mandatory Training your employer must arrange by law.
Presume capacity: support people to make their own decisions, and use the least restrictive option only as a last resort.
Make reasonable adjustments under the Equality Act 2010 — clearer communication, quieter spaces, more time — to give fair access.
Support annual health checks and hospital passports, and question over-medication through STOMP by observing and recording carefully.
A meltdown or shutdown is distress, not bad behaviour; stay calm, reduce noise and demands, and give the person time.
